reviews.title: Extremely uncomfortable experience
reviews.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆ — Extremely uncomfortable experience

I signed up for what I thought was a free trial, deleted the app that same night, and still ended up with a $7.99 charge. My card was locked, and the subscription doesn’t even show up in my Apple Subscriptions, making it difficult to figure out how to cancel it.

What made this experience even worse was the extremely personal questions the app asked me. It asked whether I live alone, whether I run every day, and whether I’m close to my neighbors. I found these questions invasive, unnecessary, and honestly really unsettling. Why does an app like this need to ask such personal questions?

Between the uncomfortable questions, the unexpected charge, and the difficulty figuring out how to cancel, this has been a terrible experience. A free trial should be clear about billing, and users should be able to easily manage and cancel subscriptions.

I would strongly encourage people to read the terms carefully before signing up and think twice about sharing personal information they’re not comfortable providing. I regret signing up and want my subscription canceled and my money refunded.

reviews.title: Beware of This App and Its Billing Practices
reviews.text:
I strongly recommend avoiding this app. I subscribed to Offender Locator but quickly discovered that someone I know is in the offender registry was missing from the results, which was extremely upsetting and made me question the accuracy of the service.

I attempted to cancel my subscription before being charged, but the app provided no way to do so. Every time I selected “Manage Subscription,” it claimed there was no subscription associated with my account.

I emailed customer support repeatedly requesting cancellation, but my requests were ignored, and I was charged $7.99 twice, even after explicitly asking them to stop billing me.

When they finally confirmed my subscription was canceled, they refused to refund either charge, despite the fact that I had requested cancellation before the charges occurred.

An app that makes it difficult to cancel, continues charging customers after cancellation requests, and then refuses refunds is unacceptable.

I have screenshots documenting everything. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this service.

reviews.title: SCAM

I tried again to cancel my subscription with the same issue. I called the contact number twice and went straight to voicemail. I had to contact my bank to dispute the charge and attempt to cancel the subscription from their end.

reviews.title: Unauthorized Charges & Nonexistent Customer Support
reviews.text:
I would strongly caution anyone against using this app. I no longer have an account, yet somehow I am STILL being charged. How is it acceptable to continue taking someone’s money when they no longer even have an account with your service?

To make matters worse, I’ve repeatedly tried contacting customer support to get this resolved, and I’ve received absolutely no response. No explanation, no refund, and no effort to address the issue.

At this point, it feels like my money is being stolen, and the company couldn’t care less. It’s beyond frustrating to be charged for a service I no longer use and then be completely ignored when I try to resolve it.

I want these charges stopped, my money refunded, and an actual response from customer support. This is completely unacceptable.

reviews.title: Free trial is extremely difficult to cancel
reviews.text:
I would NOT recommend signing up for the free trial. I tried to cancel during my free trial, but the app told me it could not find a subscription for my account. I checked my Apple subscriptions and it wasn’t listed there either, so there was literally nothing available for me to cancel.

I was then charged $7.99 anyway. After contacting support, they were suddenly able to locate and cancel the subscription, but refused to refund the $7.99 because the payment had “already been processed.”

I have screenshots showing the app saying it could not find my subscription, my Apple subscriptions showing it wasn’t listed, and the $7.99 charge.

A free trial should have a clear and functional way to cancel before being charged. Based on my experience, I strongly recommend avoiding the free trial.

reviews.title: BE VERY CAREFUL WITH THE 3-DAY FREE TRIAL
reviews.text:
I downloaded Offender Locator and signed up for the 3-day free trial. After deciding I didn’t want to continue, I tried to cancel before the trial ended.

The problem is that there is no straightforward way for me to cancel it.

The subscription does not appear under my Apple Account → Subscriptions, which is where I would normally manage a subscription started through an iPhone app. I also tried to cancel directly through the Offender Locator app, but instead I received an error telling me that I needed to contact their support team.

I did exactly that. I emailed their support team requesting cancellation, but I have received no response.

I also never received a confirmation or receipt clearly showing my subscription or explaining how it would be billed. That makes this especially concerning because I have no visible subscription in my Apple account and no working cancellation option in the app, yet the trial is apparently set up to convert into a paid subscription.

I genuinely don’t understand how I’m supposed to prevent a charge when the subscription isn’t listed with Apple, the cancellation option in the app doesn’t work, and customer support isn’t responding.

If you’re considering the 3-day free trial, please be aware of this issue and make sure you understand exactly who is billing you and how you can cancel before providing your payment information.

reviews.title: DO NOT SIGN UP FOR THE “FREE” TRIAL
reviews.text:
I would strongly advise people to STAY AWAY FROM THIS APP.

I signed up for the 3-day free trial and tried to cancel before it ended. There was no functional way to cancel through the app. The subscription wasn’t in my Apple subscriptions, and their website’s cancellation system said it sent me an email that NEVER ARRIVED. I tried multiple email addresses.

I contacted the company directly and followed every instruction they gave me. I sent them the requested email addresses and a screenshot of the charge. They then stopped responding.

The $7.99 charge went through anyway.

I had to dispute the charge with my bank, get a stop payment placed on future charges, and replace my debit card because I could not get this company to simply CANCEL A SUBSCRIPTION.

Their own Terms of Service say you can cancel by emailing them. I did that before the trial ended.

This is absolutely ridiculous.

A company should not make it this difficult to cancel a $7.99 subscription. I shouldn’t have to involve my bank and replace my debit card because a company won’t provide a working cancellation process or respond to its customers.

If you’re thinking about taking the “3-day free trial,” DON’T. The trial isn’t worth the headache of trying to get out of it.

I wish I had read the reviews before giving this company my payment information.

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text: Do not download. There is a free website to get the same information without spending the money and hassle on this app. I wanted the free trial to see if it was something I’d use. The app literally makes it impossible to cancel the subscription. There is a review down below that really helped me, but without that I’d still be trying to cancel the subscription. It’s not worth what they charge when you can get the same information for free. They are still going to try and charge me for three months even though I’ve been trying to cancel since the first day i downloaded it. I am going to have to call the bank and have them cancel any charge from this app.

reviews.title: Shady billing - don’t do the trial
reviews.text: Tried the free trial and honestly felt it wasn’t worth it, you can find this info free on the national database. It seems dated too. I tried to cancel the first day but there was absolutely no option to do so anywhere on the app. It did not show. I read another review here that they recently ran into the same problem but then it attempted to bill for the subscription and wouldn’t ya know it NOW after they tried to take the money out it gives you an option to cancel your membership within the app. Just be transparent. If you have to dupe people into paying you $8 under the guise that they can cancel anytime but making it impossible to do so you’re doing something wrong.

reviews.title: Do NOT download this app. Pretty sure it’s a scam!
reviews.text: I wanted to try the 3 day free trial to see if I wanted to use this app long term. I decided it was not worth $20 a month. There is NO way that I can find to cancel my subscription. This apparently is a very common issue. I tried to cancel before my 3 day trial ended, and there was no place to do so. I emailed customer support, and have gotten no response. This also is apparently a very common issue. Pretty sure this is a scam. It does not show up in my Apple subscriptions, yet they are charging me and saying I have a subscription. I am going to have to dispute with bank and will be reporting to Apple, I have no clue what else to do to get them to stop charging me!

reviews.title: Be cautious, very hard to cancel subscription
reviews.text:
I did the 3 day trial and when going back to cancel the subscription I wasn’t able to. I found this info from another recent review and it worked. I’m sharing their steps here!
1. Delete and redownload app
2. Once redownloaded, go through all the beginning questions again. When you get to the page about starting a subscription there will be a small “Restore” option at the bottom of the page. Click that.
3. Sign in to you Apple account.
4. A pop up will say “no subscription found, would you like to check the web?” Click yes.
5. Enter email on your Apple account
6. You will get a “manage subscription” link to your email.
7. Follow this and click cancel subscription.

A major pain, but this worked so I’m just passing along the favor!

reviews.title: Cancel subsription
reviews.text:
1. Delete and re download the app.
2. Once you re-download the app, skip all of useless advertising pages, and it’ll show you the page requiring ANOTHER SUBSCRIPTION
3. You’ll find small, tiny ‘restore’ button right below the subscription option. Click it.
4. Then it’ll require you to sign in Apple account
5. Once you put the apple account information then the pop up will show up that ‘ no subscription found, would you like to check on the web?’
6. Just click ‘yes’ and it’ll direct you to ‘manage subscription’ and will require email address on Apple account
7. Click ‘continue’ then they will send the link of ‘manage subscription’ to your email address that you confirmed on 6
8. Check your email and you can access to manage subscription
9. It’ll show you what kind of stupid subscription I had. JUST CLICK CANCELLATION.

I hope this way can help others!

reviews.title: Not completely accurate
reviews.text:
Missing information that needs to be added (it’s not new info either so it should be on here). But on top of that, I can’t even cancel my account. I’ve searched everywhere. Don’t get this app unless you are completely sure you want to keep paying for it. I’m trying to cancel after the free trial before my account is charged and it’s not showing up anywhere. There’s no emails from signing up either. Nothing in subscriptions. It’s weird. I’ve never had that happen and that feels shady. I have emailed them and will update my review if they respond.

Cancel my subscription!!!!!

reviews.title: Strong arms you into paying
reviews.text: I downloaded the app to use the advertised free version. I never got to use the app because it forced me to agree to either a free 3 day trial and then be charged $20 per month of a $2 1 month trial. No info about cancellation. The way the app begins also sets you up to prey on your fear and emotions. It’s sneaky advertising built to make you feel justified. “1.6 miles away from you!… that’s how close a predator COULD be living to you.” Spoiler alert, I know with certainty that at least 3 live on my street within walking distance. It’s gross charging people for freely available information.
